text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark is the only EU country enjoying a trade surplus with Japan thanks, to its exports of pork. Danish exports to Japan increased by almost 20 percent in the first six months of 1996 and if the trend continues, exports will get close to a total of 13 billion crowns this year.

--- Biker group Hell's Angels' new house in Copenhagen is not to be a new headquarters for the group says one of its lawyers, but merely a garage which Hell's Angels have helped establish. Speculation about a new Hells Angels base created fear among locals in the area and much political attention from prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen and minister of justice Bjoern Westh.

--- Bad quality control of Feta cheese now means that Denmark may have to pay 120 million crowns back to the European Union. Denmark received not less than four billion crowns in EU subsidies from 1990 to 1994 for its Feta which was mainly exported to Iran.

--- The first nine months of 1996 saw a considerable increase in passengers for Denmark's second largest airport at Billund in western Denmark where passengers for scheduled internaatioal flights increased by 27.2 percent to 366,000, charter passengers by 16.3 percent to 790,000 and domestic flight passengers by 4 percent to 220,000.

--- Textile companies may be forced to move production abroad to keep down expenses because of new EU taxes on textiles from the Far East used as raw materials by Danish textile producers. At the same time manufactered goods from the Far East will not be taxed and can therefore still be sold cheaply.
